client.recipe: vLLM v0.31.0 pooling runner; the stock Qwen3ForCausalLM converted to embed with is_causal false; the plugin-registered config class parses config.json locally; the checkpoint's own ST metadata resolves MEAN pooling and no activation; raw text on /v1/embeddings; the 32768-token right cut client-side

recipe.notes:
What the model is. A dense text embedder: one mean-pooled vector per text (1024 dims
at 0.6B, 2560 at 4B), no instruction and no prompt prefix (the card's model table:
"Instruction: No", "Pooling: Mean"), Matryoshka-capable (the card's "MRL: Yes"), and an
int8/binary *storage* view of the pooled vector (the card: "natively produce
*unnormalized* int8-quantized embeddings. Ensure that you compare them via *cosine
similarity*"). The checkpoint is a Qwen3 backbone whose weights were
diffusion-continued-pretrained ("All models are built on diffusion continued pre-trained
Qwen3 at Perplexity AI") and whose attention is bidirectional: modeling.py's
PPLXQwen3Model is Qwen3Model with post_init setting every layer's is_causal false and
forward building an all-to-all mask (create_causal_mask with an or_mask_function). The
sentence-transformers pipeline is Transformer -> 1_Pooling (mean tokens) ->
st_quantize.FlexibleQuantizer (the int8/binary storage step). There is no head and no
projection: the output width is the hidden size.

The serving path (established from the v0.31.0 tag source, no model class needed):
- The architecture. vLLM v0.31.0's registry carries Qwen3ForCausalLM and no
  PPLXQwen3Model (registry.py:201). The checkpoint's class is Qwen3Model with
  bidirectional attention, so the recipe pins hf_overrides {architectures:
  [Qwen3ForCausalLM], is_causal: false}: the stock Qwen3DecoderLayer reads the flag
  (qwen3.py:191-197) and builds ENCODER_ONLY attention, and a pooling runner on a
  non-pooling architecture auto-resolves to convert embed (model.py:1311).
- The config. model_type bidirectional_pplx_qwen3 is outside vLLM's _CONFIG_REGISTRY;
  the plugin registers the checkpoint's own class locally with transformers'
  AutoConfig (rcp_ndcg_vllm.models.pplx.hf_config.PplxV1Config, a plain Qwen3Config
  subclass with the model_type), so config.json parses locally and
  trust_remote_code stays false. This is the plugin's only role for this family: no
  model class registers, because the stock Qwen3ForCausalLM conversion is the model.
- The weights. The checkpoint saves the bare Qwen3Model state dict, so its tensor names
  are UNPREFIXED (embed_tokens.weight, layers.*, norm.weight; safetensors header).
  The converted pooling wrapper's loader probes the candidate prefixes ["", "model."]
  (adapters.py:189-192) and prepends model. to land them on Qwen3ForCausalLM's
  parameters; the tied lm_head (tie_word_embeddings true, no lm_head tensors) loads as
  the skipped alias.
- The pooling. The checkpoint's own ST metadata resolves the pooler: modules.json ->
  1_Pooling/config.json pooling_mode_mean_tokens true -> seq_pooling_type MEAN, and no
  Normalize module -> use_activation false (config.py:982-1063, merged at
  model.py:730-746). The engine therefore returns the unnormalized mean-pooled hidden
  state; the client L2-normalises it (cosine is scale-invariant, so the comparison is
  unaffected).
- The wire. Raw text on /v1/embeddings (request_shape text), no chat template
  (tokenizer_config.json has none), add_special_tokens a measured no-op (ByteLevel
  post-processor with no BOS/EOS template; ids(text, True) == ids(text, False)).

The reference contract (stage 2): the card's own sentence-transformers path, loaded with
trust_remote_code=True, stopped before its trailing FlexibleQuantizer. The served engine
returns the float mean-pooled vector; the quantiser is a storage format applied after
pooling, and comparing the served float vector against a lossy re-encoding would measure
the quantiser, not the serving path. The reference asserts the pipeline's module classes
(Transformer, Pooling, FlexibleQuantizer) before dropping the last, so a checkpoint
revision that changes the pipeline fails loudly. The reference's own cut derives the
card's cap from min(tokenizer_config.json model_max_length 131072, config.json
max_position_embeddings 32768) = 32768 -- exactly what sentence-transformers'
Transformer caps the tokenizer to -- and renders the card's right cut of the ids; where
the card's id cut and the client's text cut differ (an id cut inside a multi-token
character), the recipe declares over_cap_cut_differs and the harness reports those rows
non-gating. The int8 view's cosine to the float view is data-dependent (the quantiser is
round(tanh(x) * 127).clamp(-128, 127)); the wave's T3 numbers are the served float
retrieval numbers, with the card's published int8 numbers as the sanity column and any
deviation explained.

The exactly-max_model_len hang (GPU-E1, applies to both variants): the client's
max_tokens EQUALS serve.max_model_len (32768 = the model's own context; the
tokenizer's 131072 is above the model's range and is not a budget). Any pooling prompt
of exactly max_model_len tokens that is chunked never completes on vLLM v0.31.0
(GPU-E1: 32768 hangs, 32767 returns); the jina recipe's wave verified with
--max-num-batched-tokens 32768. The declared `serve.patches: [pooling-full-context]` is the remedy
(the upstream fix, exported into the engine process by the serve path); this family's two variants need it
(a request that fills the whole budget is exactly the hanging input).

The 32-bit check at max_model_len (GPU-E1's second lesson: attention q bytes and MLP
activation elements below 2^31 for one forward): at 32768 tokens, 0.6B q bytes =
32768 x 16 heads x 128 head_dim x 2 B = 134,217,728 and MLP elements = 32768 x 3072 =
100,663,296; 4B q bytes = 32768 x 32 x 128 x 2 = 268,435,456 and MLP elements =
32768 x 9728 = 318,767,104. Every number is below 2^31, so no variant needs the
32-bit warmup guard (contrast pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview, whose 262144-token
warmup overflows).

Per-size facts (each variant's own notes carry the file:key citations): the output
width is 1024 (0.6B) / 2560 (4B) -- 1_Pooling/config.json word_embedding_dimension,
equal to config.json hidden_size; the context limit is 32768 for both (config.json
max_position_embeddings; the card's 32K); the weights are float32 (config.json dtype);
and both sizes fit one 80 GB-class GPU at bf16: ~1.2 GB (596,049,920 params) / ~8.0 GB
(4,022,468,096 params) plus the KV cache (0.6B 114,688 B/token x 32768 = 3.8 GB; 4B
147,456 B/token x 32768 = 4.8 GB), so resources.gpus 1 for both.

What the GPU wave must check (NOT MEASURED on CPU):
- T0: the plugin wheel loads (pip freeze differs by exactly that wheel), the config
  parses locally (no remote code fetch; trust_remote_code stays false in the argv), and
  the engine's --max-model-len is 32768.
- T2 stage 2: served vs reference vector cosine per text (the bf16 cast is the declared
  deviation; the bidirectional ENCODER_ONLY attention is the serving contract), and the
  /tokenize equality on prompts over 32768 tokens.
- The exactly-max_model_len hang: the declared `serve.patches: [pooling-full-context]` carries the
  upstream fix into the engine process; the wave records that the full-budget request completes.
- The empty document: the client's omit_zero never sends it (the pairs generator
  records the empty-content stratum absent); a served empty prompt would be a NaN --
  assert the policy, never send one.
- The quantiser sanity: the reference's float vectors against the card's int8 view
  (round(tanh(x) * 127)) on the wave's pairs, as the T3 sanity column.

Record hygiene: every per-size number above is derived from the pinned files' headers
and keys; the wave's observations are the only place served numbers move.
Precision bounds (the E2 round-2 wave, stage 2): the reference runs the checkpoint's own fp32
(the card's SentenceTransformer passes no dtype override) while the engine serves bf16, so
stage 2's cosine gate quantifies the cast. Measured served-vs-reference minimum cosine per
variant: 0.6b 0.998196 (two of 67 vectors), 4b 0.999169 (above the published 0.999 floor). The
0.6b declares its measured floor in overrides.gates.vec_min_cosine 0.9981 (the measured
0.998196 rounds to 0.9982, which the `>=` gate would miss, so the declared bound is one step
below the rounded value); the 4b keeps the published 0.999. Every bound is declared with that
measured evidence, never defaulted; the re-run measures them again.


The 4B size (Hub API checked 2026-10-09: sha 06456497a00540a582918fe8dcd3a5eabb207772, licence mit, not gated; created 2026-01-20, card last modified 2026-06-02). Per-size facts: output width 2560 (1_Pooling/config.json word_embedding_dimension; config.json hidden_size 2560); context limit 32768 (config.json max_position_embeddings; the card's 32K); weights float32 (config.json dtype), 4,022,468,096 parameters in 398 tensors (model.safetensors header), 16,089,872,384 bytes; 36 layers, 32 attention heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, intermediate_size 9728 (config.json); bf16 weights ~8.04 GB and KV 147,456 B/token (36 x 2 x 8 x 128 x 2) x 32768 = 4.8 GB, so one 80 GB-class GPU. The 32-bit check: q bytes 32768 x 32 x 128 x 2 = 268,435,456, MLP elements 32768 x 9728 = 318,767,104, both below 2^31. The tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, configuration.py, modeling.py, modules.json and st_quantize.py are byte-identical to the 0.6B's at their pinned revisions (SHA-256); special_tokens_map.json differs only in the serialization of sep_token as a plain string instead of an object, and tokenizer_config.json (the file the engine reads) is identical. The E2 round-2 wave measured the served-vs-reference minimum cosine 0.999169, above the published 0.999 floor: this size declares no gates override (the published default holds).

vllm v0.31.0, why the stock class serves it: vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:201 -- the registry carries Qwen3ForCausalLM ('qwen3', 'Qwen3ForCausalLM') and no PPLXQwen3Model entry; vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3.py:265 Qwen3Model(Qwen2Model) and :272 Qwen3ForCausalLM; :191-197 Qwen3DecoderLayer reads getattr(config, 'is_causal', True) and builds AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY (bidirectional) when false -- the hook the recipe's hf_overrides is_causal: false drives; vllm/config/model.py:1311 the pooling-runner fallback returns convert 'embed' for a non-pooling architecture, and vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:277 wraps the class with as_embedding_model (adapters.py:250)

vllm v0.31.0, why the weight names load: vllm/model_executor/models/adapters.py:189-192 -- the converted pooling wrapper's _load_pooling_model_weights probes the candidate prefixes ['', 'model.'] against its parameter names and prepends the one that matches, so this checkpoint's UNPREFIXED tensors (embed_tokens.weight, layers.*, norm.weight; the model class is the bare Qwen3Model) land on Qwen3ForCausalLM's model.* parameters; config.json tie_word_embeddings true and the absent lm_head load as the tied alias the loader already skips (vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:202-215, :475-486)

vllm v0.31.0, the pooling and the budget: vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:982-1063 get_pooling_config reads modules.json and the pooling module's config.json (the module type table at :57-60 includes sentence_transformers.models.Pooling) and resolves pooling_mode_mean_tokens true -> seq_pooling_type MEAN with use_activation = the presence of a Normalize module (false here: the pipeline's third module is the quantiser); vllm/config/model.py:730-746 merges that base config under the user's pooler_config; vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/seqwise/poolers.py:97-105 builds the embed pooler (EmbeddingPoolerHead + PoolerNormalize) and vllm/pooling_params.py:164-168 defaults use_activation only when nothing set it, so the metadata's false stands; seqwise/methods.py:60-107 MeanPool averages over each sequence's prompt tokens

vllm v0.31.0, the config parse: vllm/transformers_utils/config.py HFConfigParser.parse (~:359-437) -- a model_type outside the engine's _CONFIG_REGISTRY goes through AutoConfig.from_pretrained with the request's trust_remote_code; the plugin's AutoConfig.register of model_type bidirectional_pplx_qwen3 (rcp_ndcg_vllm.models.pplx.hf_config.PplxV1Config, the checkpoint's own class restated) makes transformers resolve the local class and skip the remote-code branch, so trust_remote_code stays false and nothing remote runs

vllm v0.31.0, the pooling hang at exactly max_model_len: the first GPU wave's measured result -- any pooling prompt of exactly max_model_len tokens that is chunked never completes (32768 hangs, 32767 returns); the jina recipe's wave verified with --max-num-batched-tokens 32768; this family's client budget EQUALS its max_model_len, so a full-budget request is exactly that input (see the notes, 'The exactly-max_model_len hang')

sentence-transformers v6.x (the card's own dependency): sentence_transformers/base/modules/transformer.py -- __init__ caps tokenizer.model_max_length at config.max_position_embeddings when no model_max_length was passed (:874-883); the max_seq_length property reads the capped tokenizer value (:1136-1146); the text modality defaults to padding + truncation 'longest_first' (:1260) with max_length = the task cap when one is configured (none is: the checkpoint ships no sentence_bert_config.json) and the tokenizer's capped model_max_length otherwise. The reference restates exactly this cap derivation (min of tokenizer_config.json model_max_length and config.json max_position_embeddings)
